rows.reason: Line 1 'because after that there is nowhere to turn round' gives the key; 'as far as he had got' (l.4-5), 'nobody lives further out' (unstated) and 'sea wall begins there' (l.2, not a reason) are all wrong; hint locates without stating. Note: the narrator's sex is not given in the numbered lines (stems say 'he') - checkable only if the preamble states it.

Lines 4-5: twice as far as the caravan park; 'got as far as Saltmere', 'never set out' and 'walked there four years ago' all contradicted by the two lines; hint separates years from attempts without naming the key.

hintCore 'Find the bare wall. The reason is what would go on it.' states the key's content (Nan's wall is bare) rather than pointing to evidence - coaching (R572). Key and distractors otherwise check against lines 13-15.

Distractor 'He had promised Nan he would go out there' is defensible: lines 14-15 'I said I would get her a picture of the place' is a promise that can only be kept by going there; the execution's picture-not-visit distinction is too thin for a child to be marked wrong on, under a stem as open as 'what do these lines tell you about the trip'.

Line 20 'Below me a boat lay in the mud with its ribs showing through and a gull standing on it'; posts are 'further along' in the channel (l.21), the bridge is a simile (l.22), the cottages are at Saltmere (l.7); executions and tags accurate.

Lines 25-26: water behind the bank 'higher up than the field', then 'did not look over for a while' - the key is the only option giving a cause the lines support; wind dropped (l.24) rules out the wind option; 'looked over at once' contradicts l.26; hint directs to the position without stating it.

hintCore 'One word here is doing something only a plant can do' tells the child the elder is a plant, which alone selects 'a small tree or bush' from the three options - coaching (R572). Key, distractors and walkScript otherwise correct for l.29.

hintCore '... ruins. Not a result.' rules out the dominant-sense distractor that the item exists to test, leaving the key as the only feeling-word option - coaching (R572). Key 'feeling of the visit' is otherwise defensible for 'spoiled the effect' (l.32).

Key 'the water he watches is the slow one' is not supported: the passage never says standing on the step settles anything about Nan's story - a tide coming in and out over a boot (l.33-35) is not evidence for forty years of erosion over one February night (l.10-12), and the stem's 'settle' asserts a conclusion the text leaves open. Key wording ('two speeds, but...') is also hard for a 9-11 reader.

Line 37: 'a buoy in the channel that knocks when the water moves', which he decides is what she meant (l.38); tide turning is when, not what (l.36); 'nothing musical' (l.37-38) and 'no chapel on the map' (l.6) rule out the others; hint locates only.

hintCore 'Two causes, one in each line' names a property only the key has (it is the only option with two causes), so it selects the key without reading - coaching (R572). Key and distractors otherwise check against l.40-42.

hintCore 'Sort the sentences into what still stands and what happened' restates the key ('present kept for what is still true, the walk stays past') - coaching (R572). The key itself checks (l.1, 6, 8, 13, 18, 28-29, 37, 42-43 present and still true; the walk past). Distractor 2 'told it to them' has no referent for 'them'.

Lines 1-2 'it occurred to me that I should like an apple. I ran on deck'; work over is when, the watch looks out for the island, berth-restlessness unstated. Note: 'Jim' is not named in the numbered lines; relies on the passage preamble.
Line 6 'found there was scarce an apple left'; the man arrives after (l.9), straw unstated, moon at l.59; executions accurate, hint locates only.

Distractor 'He was in fear and in curiosity' is defensible: lines 11-13 have him lie there 'trembling ... in the extreme of fear', and fear is an ordinary reason for staying hidden; the item leans on the hint ('That is not why he stayed') to exclude it, which is itself coaching away the main competitor.

Line 15 'abominable old rogue' followed by Silver flattering another in the same words (l.15-16) fixes the untrustworthy sense; playful and rough-manner senses and the repetition option are wrong; hint points to evidence only. Minor: walkScript puts the flattery at l.16-17 when it starts on l.15.

Execution on 'calls Dick square / trusts him with the keg' ends 'In the window, line 22 answers the stem: 'it all away, some here, some there, and none'' - false (line 22 alone does not say how the two speeches differ) and the quote is a truncated fragment. Key otherwise checks against l.21-22 and l.44-47.

Distractor 'Silver praised him, so he agreed to join' is defensible: line 15-16 says Silver addressed the lad 'in the very same words of flattery', and that flattering talk (l.18-26) is what the lad says won him over (l.27-28); the execution only considers the later praise at l.29.

Lines 32-33: 'By a gentleman of fortune they plainly meant ... a common pirate'; the corruption and last-honest-hand options are about the scene, the map is unstated; hint narrows to 'their words' as the stem already does.

hintCore 'Read on to the end of that line' has no referent - the stem cites five lines and names none, so the child cannot tell which line is meant. Key ('hazed me long enough', l.41) and distractors otherwise check.

Line 6 puts Jim in the apple barrel and l.50-51 sends Dick for an apple, so the danger is Dick coming to his barrel; pipe-wetting is Silver's reason, guessing a boy is aboard is unstated, the terror line names the feeling; hint points to the evidence without stating the inference's answer.

'my limbs and heart alike misgave me' (l.53): with 'heart' as subject, 'misgave' carries the established sense of foreboding/doubt, so the neighbouring-sense distractor is partly supported and its execution ('line 53 fixes the sense of giving way') is not true for the heart; the hint 'Limbs cannot doubt' ignores the heart and also eliminates two distractors outright.

Lines 53-55: someone stops Dick and Hands calls for rum, addressed to John (Silver); the Silver-order, Dick-saw-Jim and Hands-scolds-Dick options are each contradicted or unstated; executions accurate.
hintCore '... He does not move' states half the key (coaching, R572); and walkScript claims 'At lines 32 and 33 he cannot move' - those lines say nothing about his movement, only his understanding.

hintCore 'Two of these are true things that happen next' is false: only the Clara-willing option is true; the wardrobe option says she found it bare, but she found rolls (l.12). Key 'decent appearance when Herr Sesemann returned' (l.5) otherwise correct.

walkScript misquotes and mislines: it gives 'bread in a wardrobe, a whole pile of bread' as line 12, but the text runs over l.12-13 and reads 'bread in a wardrobe! a whole pile of bread!'. The hat-option execution also ends in a truncated fragment ('a heap'). Key (heap of rolls, l.12) is correct.

Distractor 'Somebody took it away, and later it was in her bed' is a true answer to 'What has happened to the hat between the two?' - Tinette is ordered to take it (l.13-15) and it is found under the counterpane (l.42); the execution's 'nothing named that links them' does not make it false. Also, l.39-41 strongly imply Sebastian, so the key's 'never says who' needs care.

Lines 17-20: she took hold of Heidi rushing to stop Tinette and kept her hand on her 'to prevent her running forward'; agreeing (l.16 'No! no!'), comforting (determined tone) and the bread's-place option are wrong.

Lines 23-24 'grandmother's bread is all gone! They were all for grandmother'; heart-break is the writer's (l.25), distressed and alarmed is Clara (l.26), the mountain is unstated; hint does not select the key.

Line 29 'yours would have been hard and stale by then' - by the time she goes home, not already; replacement is the offer not the reason; the rich-house option is unstated; hint directs to the timing without stating it.

hintCore 'The word has an upon it after it. Find what the it is.' is ungrammatical and confusing for a 9-11 reader (two different 'it's in one sentence, 'the it'). Key 'trust' for 'depend upon it' (l.33) and distractors otherwise check.

Wrong window: the reason is stated at line 33 ('to make sure that she could depend upon it she kept on saying'), outside the cited lines 34-36. walkScript also says 'Line 35 puts the same question to Clara again' - line 35 is Clara's assurance.

hintCore 'Nothing here is being put down by force' eliminates the dominant-sense distractor the item tests (coaching, R572); and the 'press down hard' distractor is tagged en-figurative-taken-literally while its execution ('Built out of press') describes a built-from-parts error.

Execution on 'she saw her own roll' ends 'In the window, line 40 answers the stem: 'all sorts of strange signs, pointing to his own'' - false: the message is at line 41 ('I have got it all safe for you'); line 40 only describes the signs. Key otherwise correct.

Distractor 'She squeezes it further out of shape in her delight' is a second correct answer: 'made it more out of shape still in her joy' runs onto line 44, inside the cited window, and is something she does with the hat; the execution wrongly places it wholly at l.43.

Distractor 'What is taken is her bread, but what returns is her hat' is true of the passage and answers 'What is true of the things done to Heidi and ... for her'; and hintCore 'Look for the line where the writer gives a verdict' sends the child to search for a line that does not exist.

Lines 3-4 'set modesty aside and admit that I made a very fine figure'; dress is l.1, the King-compliment is the condition not the admission, practice unstated; hint eliminates only the clothes option.

Lines 8-9 the crowd checks his red hair and cheers; l.60-63 no one doubts him though side by side the princess would know; the helmet/no-doubt option restates without saying what it shows, princess-suspects contradicts l.60, palace plan unstated.

hintCore 'This is a thing he has, not a thing he refuses' eliminates the won't-lookalike distractor that the item exists to test - coaching (R572). Key 'usual way of looking' for 'paler than his wont' (l.11) is correct.
Line 15 'The pictures of him aren't handsome enough'; the negation-dropped pair, the manner of speaking and the prior-sighting option are all wrong; executions accurate.

'in silence and with sullen looks' (l.17-18) and the ironical portraits (l.18-19) support 'silently resentful'; 'completely silent' is the other half of the phrase, 'sullied' a lookalike, fear unstated.

Lines 19-20 give being 'spared the unpleasant sight' as the direct reason he is glad, so 'His brother's portrait was in most of the windows' (the sight) is a defensible answer alongside the temper reason. walkScript also misquotes l.20 as 'a hot temper'; the text says 'quick temper'.

Execution on the kneeling option ends 'In the window, line 24 answers the stem: 'before me, and the sudden sense of my audacity'' - false: the answer is 'Everything was in a mist as I dismounted' (l.24-25); the quoted fragment is not it. Key correct.

Execution on the oath option ends 'In the window, line 41 answers the stem: 'before them all. Then the great organ pealed out'' - false: that fragment is the organ (distractor 2), not the proclamation (l.41-42). hintCore 'The heralds say who he now is' also states the key's content.

Stem asks what the Duke's 'hands and face' show, but the key's 'looking for a way out' comes from where he looks ('to the right and to the left, as a man looks who thinks on flight', l.53-54), not his hands or face. hintCore 'Two of these describe him without saying why' is false: the Sapt option does not describe him.
Line 67 'the old man was as blind as a bat, and did not claim my acquaintance'; the dancing (l.66-67) is the danger, the ambassadors' respects not the reason, leaving-early contradicted by l.65-66.

Comments at l.11-15 each note a difference from the King, and l.17 calls them 'signs of approval and interest'; two-moments, fear (he laughs, l.8) and 'he tells us they spotted it' are not supported; hint eliminates only the two-moments option.
